newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent crude slips, other N.Sea grades slumber.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent crude slips, other N.Sea grades slumber.

text.p: Cash Brent lost ground on Friday as outright prices felt the pressure of weak U.S. product markets but North Sea wet crudes were broadly steady in extremely thin talk, traders said.
June Brent shed 30 cents to $17.99 a barrel by 1648 GMT after trading at $18.35 and $18.32 earlier in the day as U.S. gasoline and heating oil prices tumbled.
Intermonth spreads were broadly steady to a shade firmer, May/June trading twice at -20 cents in line with late Thursday's levels but June/July perked up three or four cents to trade at -8 cents.

Brent CFDs markets were almost non-existent with several players leaving early for a holiday weekend in Britain. The only real interest was in May 27-30 dates which talked slightly firmer at the equivalent of June -20/-18 cents.
North Sea spot markets were equally thin although Dated Brent drew some support from the keeping by three refiners of four cargoes nominated loading dates on Friday.
Other grades continued to talk around last done levels with traders noting little momentum in differentials in either direction.
"It looks pretty balanced at the moment," said one.
In a dull Mediterranean market, narrower refining margins pegged Russian Urals crude slightly lower at around Dated Brent -$1 per barrel, traders said.
"The deteriorating margins will dampen Mediterranean refiner buying, but avails are not too lengthy so sellers can stay relaxed for a while," one trader said.
West African crude markets were also quiet but steady as good Asian and transatlantic demand balanced lighter Mediterranean interest.
Traders said sweeter West African grades were supported by ongoing demand from Far East refiners topping up after a recent lengthy spell of maintenance and transatlantic buying.

Prices for distillate-rich but seasonally out of favour Forcados were also stable at around Dated Brent +10 cents but traders said they could slip a little if supportive European demand subsides on the back of the narrowing margins.
Buying for June FOB barrels was becoming the focus of interest with May cargoes mostly tied up.
"The market should stay pretty firm in the near term but we may see the usual price volatility when NNPC starts pricing for June," one trader said.
Bonny Light was valued around Dated Brent +47 cents a barrel following trade on Thursday for a May 25-27 loading cargo at the level.
-- Mark Thompson, Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
